counterexample: Tick spacing 60. The only position is [600, 1200), so no tick at or below 0 is initialized. Start 0, end -120. The walk should return nothing. reset keeps loading lower words until wordPos reaches type(int16).min, about 32,769 calls to the pool manager, and runs out of gas. The post-hoc check test_check_taxedSwapDownWithNoInitializedTickBelow measured 148,912,501 gas for such a swap, so it cannot fit in a block.

new_flaw.description: The search loop in reset never compares the scanned word with the end tick. A taxed zero-for-one swap that starts below every initialized tick needs about 149 million gas and reverts. When an initialized tick exists but lies far below the end tick, each reset still loads every word down to it, for example about 3,466 words in a spacing-1 pool whose nearest lower tick is a full-range position at -887272, and the hook calls reset twice per swap.

claude-opus-5-5.reason: The loop only stops at a set bit or at type(int16).min, never at the end tick, and the post-hoc gas check measured about 149 million gas for a taxed swap with no initialized tick below.

gpt-6.1-sol.reason: For an empty range there is no walk to begin and hasNext is already false, and the audited code and the reference repair also return before loading a word, so this is not a real break of point 7.

summary: Rewrites reset with its own loop that searches from the start tick's own bit, so an initialized start tick is returned. The loop keeps loading lower words until it finds any initialized tick or reaches the lowest word, and never stops at the end tick.
